---
title: "Normalization"
---

After [quality control](qc.html), decide whether your quantities need any further
adjustment before comparing conditions.

::: {.alert .alert-info role="note"}
**DIA-NN usually normalizes already:** DIA-NN reports normalized quantities by
default, so an additional normalization step is optional. You can continue with
the imported matrix if it suits your analysis. See the
[DIA-NN documentation](https://github.com/vdemichev/DiaNN#quantification).
:::

If an additional adjustment is useful, ProteoVaultR provides **stable-reference
normalization**. It selects abundant protein groups measured in every sample and
uses their collective abundance to calculate a scaling factor for each sample.

The examples below continue with the HepG2 protein-group `se` from
[Preparing data](preparing-data.html). Use its original `quantity` assay without
log-transforming it first; the functions handle that internally.

```{r setup, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(ProteoVaultR)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
    collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5,
    dev.args = list(bg = "white")
)
data_dir <- Sys.getenv("PROTEOVAULTR_DEMO_DIR", unset = "demo-data")
vault <- open_vault(
    file.path(data_dir, "hepg2_ifna-dia.proteovault.duckdb")
)
sample_info <- tibble::tribble(
    ~sample_name,   ~sample_id, ~condition,
    "Control_R1",  "Ctrl1",    "Control",
    "Control_R2",  "Ctrl2",    "Control",
    "Control_R3",  "Ctrl3",    "Control",
    "IFNa_12h_R1", "IFNa1",    "IFNa",
    "IFNa_12h_R2", "IFNa2",    "IFNa",
    "IFNa_12h_R3", "IFNa3",    "IFNa"
)
sample_info$condition <- factor(
    sample_info$condition, levels = c("Control", "IFNa")
)
vault <- set_sample_metadata(vault, sample_info)
se <- as_summarized_experiment(vault, method = "matrix")
close_vault(vault)
```

## 1. Apply stable-reference normalization

The geNorm-style method selects proteins with stable abundance ratios to one
another. Normalize a copy of `se`, then inspect the adjustment:

```{r genorm-normalization, fig.alt="Before-and-after profiles of selected geNorm reference proteins against all completely measured proteins in the HepG2 DIA dataset."}
se_genorm <- normalize_stable_reference_genorm(se)
plot_stable_reference_diagnostics(se_genorm)
```

Gray violins show the proteins measured in every sample. Blue profiles and boxes
show the selected references. Each protein's log2 abundance is centered on its
own mean across samples, so the panels show relative sample patterns before and
after normalization. The before-and-after profiles are very similar in this demo.

The result adds `quantity_genorm_normalized` while preserving the original
`quantity` assay. The normalized quantities remain on the intensity scale.

Reference selection does not use the sample conditions. Inspect the broader
protein distribution as well as the references: closer alignment of the selected
references is expected because they were used to calculate the adjustment. It
does not establish that they are biologically unchanged.

PCA-based reference selection is also available through
`normalize_stable_reference_pca()`; see its function reference for the selection
settings.

## 2. Continue with your chosen quantities

If you keep the additional normalization, use `quantity_genorm_normalized` in
subsequent analysis. Otherwise, continue with the original `quantity` assay.

This step does not impute missing values. In the new normalized assay, zeros are
treated as missing and existing missing values remain missing. Next, see
[Missing values](missing-values.html) before testing differences between conditions.
